forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For every real number x, x = floor(x) + frac(x), and 0 <= frac(x) < 1.

payload.previous_feedback: Previous vetter reason: The proof matches the lemma exactly: it states the standard identity frac(x) = x - floor(x) for all real x. No substantive gap, drift, or illegal dependency is present.
payload.previous_proof_nl: For any real number x, frac(x) denotes the fractional part of x. By the defining identity for the fractional part, frac(x) is exactly the remainder after subtracting the floor of x, namely x - floor(x). Hence for every real x, frac(x) = x - floor(x).
payload.role_in_assembly: Identifies the fractional part with the floor-remainder expression so that the inequality and equality lemmas can be rewritten into statements about frac(x).

payload.statement_nl: For every real number x, frac(x) = x - floor(x).

result_payload.addressed_previous_feedback: I kept the same definition-based proof from the previous attempt, since the vetter confirmed it already matched the lemma exactly and used no improper dependency.
result_payload.proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By the definition of the fractional-part function frac, its value at x is x minus the greatest integer less than or equal to x, namely floor(x). Therefore frac(x) = x - floor(x), as claimed.
result_payload.proof_summary: The lemma is exactly the defining identity of the fractional-part function: for every real x, frac(x) is x - floor(x).
